$schema_note: AWS EventBridge rule + target definitions for ReciterAI Phase 10 (D-10). Single-file IaC; promoted to CDK only when the migration threshold in infra/README.md fires.

rules.name: reciterai-hot-weekly
rules.description: Hot path: weekly Step Functions execution covering score -> assign -> rollup over delta PMIDs. Cron locked 2026-05-12 per Open Q 10.1 (ReciterDB daily refresh confirmed).
rules.schedule_comment: Mondays 12:00 UTC = 08:00 EDT. Lands after typical overnight ReciterDB refresh; inside US business hours for pager response. Override: edit this rule + redeploy via scripts/deploy_cron.sh.

rules.name: reciterai-spotlight-monthly
rules.description: Spotlight refresh: monthly ECS Fargate RunTask (#329 shape a2) running the dirty-check gate (D-03); if thresholds trip, regenerates the spotlight via backfill_spotlight.py --publish. Fargate, not Lambda: the regen runs the full cli.backfill_spotlight (whole repo + LLM deps, past the 15-min ceiling). EventBridge Input is not forwarded to ECS targets, so the invocation is the task definition's default command (infra/spotlight_task_definition.json).
rules.schedule_comment: 1st of each month, 13:00 UTC = 09:00 EDT. One hour after the hot path so the dirty-check sees STAGE# rows from the most recent hot run.

rules.name: reciterai-drift-daily
rules.description: Drift evaluator: daily Lambda invocation. Reads UNCOVERED_PMID#, LOW_CONFIDENCE_ASSIGNMENT#, and STAGE#...failed rows over drift_window_days; writes DRIFT#evaluation; dispatches severity-tagged Teams alerts via pipeline_enrichment.alerting (T11; migrated from pipeline_common.alert on the 2026-05-25 deploy).
rules.schedule_comment: Daily 14:00 UTC = 10:00 EDT. Two hours after the hot path, one hour after the spotlight rule, so all upstream STAGE# rows for the most recent run are in place before the rolling 14-day window is evaluated.

rules.name: reciterai-onboarding-detector-daily
rules.description: Onboarding detector: daily Lambda invocation (#80 Phase 2). Faculty-scoped publication gap scan + ReCiter attribution-churn check; files a GitHub issue per flagged CWID and posts a Teams digest. Does NOT invoke the onboarding state machine (#80 D1 — issue-filing only).
rules.schedule_comment: Daily 13:00 UTC = 09:00 EDT. Morning business hours after the overnight ReciterDB refresh, so filed issues + the Teams digest land at the operator's day-start. No ordering dependency on the weekly hot run or the 14:00 drift run — a standalone faculty scan over ReciterDB + DynamoDB PROCESSING#/rollup rows. Override: edit this rule + redeploy via scripts/deploy_cron.sh.

rules.name: reciterai-enrichment-daily
rules.description: Daily enrichment: scheduled ECS Fargate RunTask invocation (#37 PR 4). Generates `reciterai_synopsis` + `reciterai_impact` rows in MariaDB and `IMPACT#` rows in DynamoDB for new WCM-faculty publications since the last successful tick. Bedrock Claude Sonnet 4.6 on the happy path; OpenAI gpt-5.1 on the content-filter fallback (D3).
rules.schedule_comment: Daily 11:00 UTC = 07:00 EDT. Slot picked to land after the overnight ReciterDB refresh and BEFORE the onboarding detector (13:00 UTC) so its faculty gap scan sees the morning's freshly-enriched papers; also before drift (14:00 UTC). Override: edit this rule + redeploy via scripts/deploy_cron.sh.

rules.name: reciterai-taxonomy-drift-daily
rules.description: Taxonomy/data drift check (ADR D5 layer 2). Scans the TOPIC# partition space and compares it two-way against the bundled taxonomy_v2.json: orphan partitions (a topic still being scored after retirement) and unscored topics (a topic added but never reaching prod). Writes DRIFT#taxonomy; dispatches WARN/ERROR Teams cards via pipeline_enrichment.alerting. Distinct from reciterai-drift-daily, which evaluates model-quality drift and owns DRIFT#evaluation.
rules.schedule_comment: Daily 15:00 UTC = 11:00 EDT. One hour after the drift evaluator so the two daily checks do not contend, and 21 hours ahead of the Monday cron(0 12 ? * MON *) hot run — the ADR requires this check to land before the weekly scoring pass, since that pass is what re-mints rows for retired topics.
rules.state_comment: ENABLED 2026-08-06, once the precondition below was met. The precondition is retained because it recurs on every rebuild of this rule: deploy_cron.sh only wires the trigger — it will happily bind a target to a non-existent ARN, swallow the add-permission failure ('permission already present'), and exit 0, so an ENABLED rule whose function does not exist fails silently every day. The function must exist first. Required config, mirroring reciterai-drift-evaluator: handler pipeline_taxonomy_drift.checker.handler, python3.12, Timeout 300, Memory 512, env RECITERAI_TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL (without it alerting.alert returns False; the finding is still persisted to the DRIFT# row and logged, but only at INFO, and the invocation still returns green — see alert_sent on the row, added in #359). Measured on the first real invocation 2026-08-06: 9.2s, 97MB peak, 69 partitions vs 69 taxonomy topics, severity OK. That runtime confirms the 3s Lambda default would time out; 300 is correct and the table only grows.

rules.name: reciterai-grants-daily
rules.description: Grant-opportunity ingest: daily ECS Fargate RunTask (#269) running the grants.gov sweep then the SPS submission-queue drain (pipeline_grants.ingest; pipeline_grants.ingest_submissions — chained with ';' so a grants.gov failure still drains the queue). EventBridge Input is not forwarded to ECS targets, so the invocation is the task definition's default command (infra/grants_task_definition.json). SPIN ingest is deliberately excluded (ingest_spin decision #5 — no scheduler until the ToS check clears).
rules.schedule_comment: Daily 03:00 UTC = 23:00 EDT. Overnight slot: launches 4h before SPS's 07:00 nightly projection reads the GRANT# rows and 8h before the 11:00 UTC enrichment tick — no contention with the other ECS crons. Completion inside that 4h window is an assumption, not a measurement (hours-class sweep, one Bedrock call per kept item, no Fargate timeout); measure the first full sweep's wall clock against 07:00 (README first-tick step) and, if it overruns, move the cron earlier or the drain first. Override: edit this rule + redeploy via scripts/deploy_cron.sh.

rules.name: reciterai-cores-daily
rules.description: Core-facility usage inference: daily ECS Fargate RunTask over core 14 (Research Informatics) ONLY, running `python -m pipeline_cores.run --core 14 --with-affinity --alias-search --llm-carry-forward`. Re-scores that core against the whole ReciterDB corpus and writes the surfaced confirmed/candidate rows to DynamoDB, which is what SPS's core claim queue reads. Makes ZERO Bedrock calls. See description_note below for the deliberate flag omissions.
rules.description_note: Kept OUT of `description` because EventBridge caps PutRule.Description at 512 chars and deploy_cron.sh passes the field straight through — botocore does not enforce the cap client-side, so an oversized description survives `--dry-run` and only fails on the real put-rule, aborting the script before put-targets (the same trap tests/test_infra_eventbridge_shape.py was written for after the 2026-08-07 spotlight deploy). The omissions this rule depends on: `--with-llm` is deliberately absent — a corpus-wide LLM pass is ~80k Haiku screens a night (run.py persists only confirmed/candidate rows, so 79,860 of the 80,203 corpus publications carry no stored score on any given night), and how much Bedrock a nightly may spend is an open decision in its own issue. `--llm-carry-forward` re-emits the stored LLM evidence that persist.put_core_usage would otherwise REMOVE from every row it re-surfaces (#384); without it the first tick would strip the review queue's strongest chip off all 62 open core-14 rows. Full rationale in infra/cores_task_definition.json deploy_notes.llm_evidence_and_bedrock. Other cores stay operator-run; this rule cannot touch their rows.
rules.schedule_comment: Daily 05:00 UTC = 01:00 EDT. The slot is chosen by ORDERING, not by convenience, and it is sandwiched between two fixed points. (a) Two hours BEFORE SPS's own cron(0 7 * * ? *) nightly, which is the job that projects the CORE# rows into MySQL for display — a night's scoring has to land before SPS reads it, or the queue shows yesterday's chips for another 24h. (b) Two hours AFTER the grants tick starts (03:00 UTC). These are separate Fargate tasks with separate task roles, so they contend for nothing in-process; the only resource they could share is the Bedrock rate, and this command uses none of it. That makes the 03:00 spacing courtesy rather than a constraint, while the 07:00 deadline is real. MEASURED 2026-09-05, before the rule was enabled: a full-corpus pass over 80,245 publications plus the two paginated DynamoDB Scans ran on Fargate in ~42 seconds, against a 2h window — roughly 170x headroom, so the ordering below is not tight. That said there is still no Fargate task timeout to bound a hung run (a stalled NCBI socket is the likeliest cause), so an overrun would be unbounded rather than late. Re-measure if the corpus or the signal set grows materially. If it ever overruns, move THIS cron earlier — never the SPS nightly, which has its own downstream consumers and ordering; this rule is the newest and cheapest thing in the chain to move. Override: edit this rule + redeploy via scripts/deploy_cron.sh.

deploy_notes.templating: {account_id} is read from $AWS_ACCOUNT_ID at deploy time. {region} resolves from the top-level region field. scripts/deploy_cron.sh handles substitution before passing to aws CLI.
deploy_notes.iam: Each target ARN assumes its IAM role exists: reciterai-eventbridge-invoke-states for the Step Functions target, the Lambda execution role attached to the named function for the Lambda targets, and reciterai-eventbridge-invoke-ecs for the ECS RunTask targets (Fargate enrichment + spotlight + grants + cores — its policy must allow ecs:RunTask on ALL FOUR task-definition families and iam:PassRole for each task/execution role pair; the per-family omission has bitten on every new family, cores included until step 3 of its README launch path is done — see infra/README.md). Minimum policies are documented in infra/lambda_iam_policy.json (Lambdas), infra/enrichment_task_iam_policy.json (enrichment task role), infra/cold_run_task_iam_policy.json (the reciterai-cold-task role, which the spotlight task reuses — it already scopes S3 write to wcmc-reciterai-artifacts/spotlight/*), infra/grants_task_iam_policy.json (the reciterai-grants-task role — S3 scoped to wcmc-reciterai-artifacts/grants/*), and infra/cores_task_iam_policy.json (the reciterai-cores-task role — DynamoDB + CloudWatch Logs only, no S3 and no SecretsManager; the smallest of the four).
deploy_notes.ecs_targets: ECS targets need RECITERAI_ENRICHMENT_SUBNETS and RECITERAI_ENRICHMENT_SECURITY_GROUPS env vars at deploy time (comma-separated). Subnets must reach ReciterDB; security groups must permit egress to Bedrock + OpenAI + MariaDB + Secrets Manager (the grants task uses only the Bedrock + AWS-API egress plus HTTPS to grants.gov and submitted opportunity URLs; the cores task needs MariaDB to ReciterDB, the AWS API for DynamoDB, and HTTPS to eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov + www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov for the --alias-search PMC lookups — it needs no Bedrock egress on the scheduled command, but leave it reachable so an operator --with-llm override works without a security-group change). Reuse the hot-path Lambdas' VPC layout — same network requirements.
deploy_notes.override_cadence: All cron expressions are tunable here without code changes. Change the schedule_expression, re-run scripts/deploy_cron.sh, and EventBridge picks up the new schedule within ~1 minute.
